notes: Candidate fixes for the Analyze handoff's ranked verified causes, built 2026-08-07. Two candidates compete for the top-ranked cause chain (the drink-queue pileup and its one-head/batch-locked root, 55% of delay tallies): a method change on the head that exists (batch milk steaming + marked-cup sequencing) and the capital fix (a second machine head). One candidate attacks the #2 cause (grinder rework, 25%): a backup grinder + dose dial-in routine. Criteria and weights were declared 09:40, scores entered 11:10 -- weights before scores, and the engine's timestamps show the order. Every rating's basis is stated in its solution description; the arithmetic (quadrants, weighted totals, ranking) is the engine's. The honest loser: the second machine head carries the highest gap impact on the board (5) and still ranks last -- a ~$12k two-group machine plus install weeks against a $40 method change; it stays on the ranked list as the escalation path if the method changes cannot close the gap, not as a rejected idea. The ranked list is the Improve queue: #1 goes to the round-1 pilot (T-19) alone; #2 waits for the round-1 proof's remaining-gap check.

solutions.name: Batch milk steaming + marked-cup sequencing at the drink-build step
solutions.description: Method change at the espresso station, no new equipment beyond a second large pitcher (~$40 with rail labels): scan the next three marked cups for a same-milk pair before each build; for a pair, pull both drinks' shots back-to-back while one shared pitcher steams, and build cups strictly in ticket order from a marked front-of-rail position. Attacks the verified root directly -- one machine head with batch sizes locked to one drink at a time (c-batch-locked) -- and the 4.5-minute drink-queue wait that root produces (c-queue, 55% of the 40 delay tallies, the Pareto's biggest vital-few bar). Impact rated 4: the queue is the largest single block of the 8.41-minute baseline, and milk drinks are ~80% of orders (latte 40 + cappuccino 25 + mocha 15), so pairing opportunities are frequent. Effort rated 2: a training conversation, a laminated card, and a marked rail -- startable Monday. Cost scored 5 (near-zero spend); speed scored 4 (one week of paired-shift practice); gap-impact scored 4.

solutions.name: Backup grinder + dose dial-in routine
solutions.description: One dosing method change built around a standby unit: dial in the grinder before peak and re-dial after every hopper refill; when the primary drifts mid-peak, swap in the dialed-in backup grinder instead of re-dialing with cups waiting. Attacks grinder rework re-pulls (c-grinder, 10 of 40 delay tallies, 25% -- the second vital-few bar), each re-pull restarting a drink and stalling every cup behind it (~2 minutes, FMEA r-repull's cause: grind drift after hopper refills). Impact rated 3: it recovers the rework share of the gap, not the queue itself. Effort rated 2: dining services has a compatible refurbished grinder (~$300) and the routine is a card plus a log. Cost scored 4; speed scored 4 (needs the unit transferred and dialed); gap-impact scored 3.

solutions.name: Second espresso machine head (replace with a two-group machine)
solutions.description: The capital fix for the same root the batching change attacks: a two-group machine doubles head capacity so two drinks progress in parallel (c-one-head, c-station-serial -- the fishbone's 'change the batching or add head capacity' fork, taken the equipment way). Impact rated 5: it removes the serial constraint outright instead of working around it. Effort rated 5 and cost scored 1: roughly $9-14k for the machine, plumbing and electrical install, counter re-layout, and an estimated two weeks of disrupted service -- Dana's budget cycle could not fund it before spring. Speed scored 1; gap-impact scored 5. Ranked honestly, not picked: it loses to the method change on cost/effort/speed while the method change is available at $40, and it stays on the list as the known escalation if the gap will not close without new capacity.

criteria.name: Gap impact -- how much of the 3.41-minute gap this can recover (5 = attacks the largest verified block)
Effort and speed to implement (5 = startable within a week with training only, 1 = weeks of install and disruption)

provenance.method: quadrant = impact/effort each split at the 1-5 scale's midpoint (>=3 high, <3 low); weighted_total = sum(score * weight) over criterion_scores when a solution has scored every declared criterion, else None (nothing to weight yet -- schema guarantees criterion_scores is all-or-nothing per solution)
